sample_unit: laboratory value readings from a synthetic document (plus 1,988 held-out readings from 20 reports)

links.outcome: Share of corrupted extracted values caught by two-reader agreement check, and review rate
links.effect: Agreement between two independently built readers caught 193 of 193 corruptions on held-out data at a 19.8% review rate.
links.quote: Requiring agreement between two independently built readers caught 193 of 193 corruptions on held-out data at a 19.8% review rate.

links.outcome: Laboratory value misreads under controlled image degradation
links.effect: At 100 dpi, character accuracy remained at 88.9% while 32.3% of laboratory values were misread; 89 of 188 corrupted values (47.3%) carried the same abnormality flag as the truth.
links.quote: At 100 dpi, character accuracy remained at 88.9% while 32.3% of laboratory values were misread.

links.outcome: Whether character-level accuracy reveals value-level errors and flag-level safety
links.effect: Character accuracy stayed high while many values were misread. Silent corruption was more common for already-abnormal values (61.7% vs 22.1%; risk ratio 2.80, 95% CI 1.75 to 4.47).
links.quote: Character-level accuracy is not a safety metric for pipelines that reduce measurements to flags, and the errors such pipelines hide fall disproportionately on patients whose values are already abnormal.

links.outcome: Fine-tuned recogniser accuracy on its tuning document versus held-out reports with unseen fonts
links.effect: Fine-tuned model read its tuning document perfectly at low resolution but lost 8.1 percentage points against its base model on held-out reports (unadjusted p = 0.031).
links.quote: Fine-tuning the recogniser did not help: it read the document it was tuned for perfectly at low resolution, but against its own base model under identical preprocessing it lost 8.1 percentage points on held-out reports (unadjusted p = 0.031; this and the corresponding version 1 comparison do not survive correction for multiple testing).

unlisted_practices: Upscaling document images before recognition to improve value extraction accuracy
Evaluating value-level and flag-level (alert-relevant) errors rather than character-level accuracy in document extraction pipelines

screen.practice: dual-reader consensus verification and image upscaling pre-processing
screen.reason: The study empirically tests specific safeguards (dual-reader agreement/consensus verification check and image upscaling) to detect and prevent silent numerical corruption in clinical document extraction pipelines.
